Title: LSJ: Q about Mask of a Thousand Faces & Approximation of Loyalty

Messages.Author: dead...@yahoo.com
Messages.Body:
When you want to "cancel a card as it is played," can you do
something (eg. play card(s), tap card(s) for effect. ) before you do
the cancellation?

More specifically, can you play "Approximation of Loyalty" at
superior after playing "Mask of a Thousand Faces"?

For example: (Consider Jack, Jane, Joe, to be Vampires with appropriate
Capacity & Disciplines.)
I tap Jack to Bleed. My prey plays Deflection with Jane. Joe takes over
Jack with "Mask" and play "Approximation" to cancel the
"Deflection." (Because Joe has the ability to use
"Approximation" but Jack doesn't, for instance.)
Is this legal?

Mask of a Thousand Faces
Cardtype: Action Modifier / Discipline: Obfuscate
Only usable by a ready, untapped vampire other than the acting minion
who is capable of performing the action. Not usable if any action
modifiers or other effects have been used that could not have been used
if this vampire were the acting vampire.
[obf] Untap the acting minion and tap this vampire instead. Now this
vampire is the acting minion. The action resumes where it left off.
[OBF] As above, with +1 stealth.

Approximation of Loyalty
Cardtype: Action Modifier / Cost: 1 blood / Discipline: Presence
Requires a vampire with capacity above 6.
[pre] Only usable when the action is announced. Choose a vampire with
capacity below 7 or an ally. That minion cannot block this action.
[PRE] Cancel a reaction card played by a vampire with capacity below 7
or an ally as it is played (no cost is paid). No more action modifiers
can be played on this action.

Messages.Author: Greg
Messages.Body:


I would say no, though I found an old thread the other day that
suggests LSJ might overrule me on this. To play a cancel effect, you
have to play it immediately, before there is a chance to tap the
Barrens, play an Action Modifier or Reaction, before even you replace
it. Several cards have "Do Not Replace" clauses as part of their
effect, so you should have to determine if a card is cancelled before
you have the opportunity to replace it. More to your point, you can't
play Mask until their card has taken effect, which means you'd have to
play Approximation first.

--
- Gregory Stuart Pettigrew
